sections.h2: Where is West Fargo, North Dakota, and how big is it?
sections.html:
West Fargo is a city in Cass County that sits immediately west of Fargo and belongs to the Fargo-Moorhead metropolitan area. It covers about 16.4 square miles at an elevation of 899 feet, and the Census Bureau estimates 41,175 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 38,626 at the 2020 census.

Interstate 94, U.S. 10 and U.S. 52 serve the city. West Fargo works with the North Dakota Department of Transportation, the Fargo-Moorhead Metropolitan Council of Governments and Fargo Moorhead Metro Area Transit on transportation planning. A five-member City Commission, led by the mayor, governs the city.

sections.h2: What is the history of West Fargo?
sections.html:
West Fargo started as a whistle stop on the Northern Pacific Railway called Sheyenne Crossing, named for the nearby Sheyenne River. The settlement was later renamed Haggartville and then Haggart after John E. Haggart, who owned the land and served as postmaster, U.S. Marshal and the first sheriff of Cass County. The first school was built in 1876.

In 1919 a group of farmers formed the Equity Co-op Packing Company and built a meat processing plant. After it went bankrupt in 1922, Armour and Company bought it in 1925, and the settlement became the Village of West Fargo. The Armour plant closed in 1960, and the high school teams are still called the Packers. West Fargo became a city in 1967 and merged with Riverside in 1989.

The city's village years, 1930 to 1967, and its incorporation as a city in 1967 mark the later stages of that growth.

sections.h2: Which school district serves West Fargo homes?
sections.html:
West Fargo Public Schools serves the city of West Fargo, much of southwestern Fargo, Reile's Acres, and the communities of Horace and Harwood.

The district's high schools are West Fargo High School, Sheyenne High, Horace High and Community High. Taxes tie to the district too, because the Cass County levy list shows different combined rates for the City of West Fargo with the West Fargo School District and for other city and school combinations.

sections.h2: What property taxes must be paid before a West Fargo house can close?
sections.html:
In Cass County, all current-year property taxes must be paid in full before a deed can be recorded to transfer ownership. That is a direct requirement on the seller, so plan for it when you schedule a closing, especially in the early months of the year when taxes become due.

If a deadline falls on a weekend or county holiday, it moves to the next business day. The 2025 statements were mailed on December 12, 2025, with the discount available through February 17, 2026. Contact the county Finance Office at 701-241-5600 or taxes@casscountynd.gov if a statement does not arrive. These dates are on the Cass County property tax page.

sections.h2: How is the tax calculated, and what credits are available?
sections.html:
Cass County follows the state formula: the assessor sets true and full value, assessed value is 50 percent of that, and taxable value for residential property is 4.5 percent of true and full value. The county then applies the mill levy for your taxing district. The county's published example shows a $300,000 home owing $3,881.38 in net consolidated tax under its sample levy.

  • New construction may qualify for a two-year abatement that takes $150,000 off true and full value for figuring real estate tax. The county's example drops the same $300,000 home to $1,940.69. The abatement does not reduce special assessments or drain taxes.
  • The Primary Residence Credit can reduce the tax obligation by up to $1,600 for an eligible homeowner with an approved application.
  • The county's calculator lists a levy of 306.19 mills for the City of West Fargo. Levies change each year, so use your own statement.

The West Fargo assessor reappraises periodically, and the city says any change from a reappraisal appears on the tax bill you receive the following December. A typical appraisal visit takes 15 to 20 minutes and includes an indoor and outdoor inspection.

sections.h2: How do special assessments work in West Fargo?
sections.html:
West Fargo uses special assessments, authorized by Chapter 40 of the North Dakota Century Code, to charge property owners for infrastructure that benefits their land. The city's examples include water lines and storage, sewer lines, storm sewer, road and sidewalk paving, and flood protection.

  • The unpaid, uncertified balance is the amount left after each year's installment goes to Cass County. You can look up a property's balance on the city's assessor website by address or parcel number.
  • Pending specials are estimates for projects still under construction or not yet through final hearings, so the amount can change.
  • To pay off a balance, contact the Finance department or submit a Special Assessment Payoff Request. Interest accrues monthly, so you need an actual payoff figure.
  • The city accepts no specials payments between October 1 and November 10, so it can certify installments to the county.
  • The city does not hold information for the Sheyenne Diversion, which has its own contact at 701-298-2381.

Request payoff numbers early, because a balance generally has to be addressed at closing. The details are on the city's finance FAQ.

sections.h2: What city steps come with moving out of a West Fargo house?
sections.html:
West Fargo bills water, sewer, garbage and other services monthly, and the bill stays in your name until you end service. To stop utilities when you sell, complete the Utility Service Move Out Application with your forwarding address, your closing or moving date, and the new owner's name.

Building permits are handled at the Building Department at 2515 Sixth Street E, and the city's building code requires permits before certain construction on existing structures. Fees are based on the value of the project, and mechanical permits depend on the type, size and number of appliances. If you finished a basement, replaced a furnace or added a deck, gather the permit records before you list.

sections.h2: What does flood protection mean for a West Fargo home?
sections.html:
Flood control is a large regional project around West Fargo. The Metro Flood Diversion Authority's project is described in Cass County's audited financial report as providing flood protection for approximately 200,000 people in North Dakota and Minnesota. Voters in Fargo and Cass County approved two dedicated local sales taxes, expected to raise $700 million over the life of the tax.

The city also lists flood protection among the improvements that can be paid for through special assessments, and its finance staff refer Sheyenne Diversion questions to a separate office. If your lender or buyer asks about flood status, check the current map and your assessment statements, and keep records of any flood-related work. West Fargo has a humid continental climate, with large seasonal swings that make roofing, sump pumps and heating the usual inspection topics.

sections.h2: What must I disclose, and what are my selling options in West Fargo?
sections.html:
North Dakota requires a seller of a residential dwelling with up to four units to provide a written disclosure of material facts before the buyer signs final acceptance, under N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1. The statute exempts foreclosure sales, sales by estate fiduciaries and transfers to close relatives. Section 47-10-02.2 adds a radon disclosure, and section 47-10-02.3 requires homeowners association documents within ten days of a signed agreement.

West Fargo sellers can list with an agent, sell on their own or accept a cash offer from a buyer that purchases as-is. If your house is under a tight deadline, such as an inherited property or a pending move, compare the net proceeds after taxes, special assessments and payoff of any liens. Cash Home Buyers can review a West Fargo address and explain how an offer works. We do not quote prices here, and you owe nothing if you decline.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay all property taxes before selling in West Fargo?
faqs.a: In Cass County, all current-year property taxes must be paid in full in order to record a deed that transfers ownership. Ask your title company for the exact figure early in the process.

faqs.q: When are Cass County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Statements are mailed in December, and taxes are due January 1. The first installment is due March 1 and the second October 15, with a 6 percent penalty on a late second installment. A 5 percent discount applies if taxes are paid in full by February 15.

faqs.q: Which school district covers West Fargo?
faqs.a: West Fargo Public Schools serves the city of West Fargo, much of southwestern Fargo, Reile's Acres, Horace and Harwood. High schools include West Fargo High School, Sheyenne High, Horace High and Community High.

faqs.q: How do I find my special assessment balance in West Fargo?
faqs.a: Search the city's assessor website by parcel number or address. For a payoff amount, contact the city Finance department or use the Special Assessment Payoff Request form, because interest accrues monthly.

faqs.q: Does West Fargo require anything when I move out?
faqs.a: You should submit the Utility Service Move Out Application, including your closing date and the new owner's name if you are selling. Otherwise the utility bill remains in your name.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Fargo house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You still owe the buyer the written disclosures required by North Dakota law, and a buyer that purchases as-is decides whether to accept the property in its current condition.
